notes:
Quick summary: Ridgeview is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for customer-facing chat + reranking for product search. Primary constraint is strict latency: customer research shows users notice delays >300ms for chat replies. They want a predictable reserve (monthly) with throughput guarantee for peak shopping hours.

Recent timeline / activity (bullets):
- 2026-02-20: Intro call (Maya) — overview of use cases, flagged strict SLO needs.
- 2026-02-28: Technical deep-dive (SE Diego + infra) — shared sample traffic profiles + 95th/99th tail concerns; provided load traces. (ff_20260228_3910)
- 2026-03-05: Capacity sizing workshop — Redwood suggested 8x GPUs with continuous batching enabled for target throughput; discussed streaming instrumentation (ff_20260305_4452).
- 2026-03-09: Pricing follow-up, legal kickoff for SLA.

Use-case & requirements (shorthand):
- Workloads: low-latency chat (streaming), search rerank (non-streaming, batched), embeddings for indexing.
- Targets: customer wants p50/p95/p99 SLAs; suggested targets from Ridgeview: chat TTFB p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 150ms, p99 <= 300ms; chat per-token tail p95 <= 120ms; non-streaming rerank (end-to-end) p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 450ms.
- Throughput: baseline steady-state 120 req/s for 512-token average context during peak; burst-to-peak 350 req/s for short windows.
- Cost sensitivity: wants quantized bound on $/1M tokens; preferred blended committed rate.
- Deploy: VPC + SSO/SAML; audit logs retained 1 year; KMS-backed key management.

Latency SLO definition & measurement alignment (notes for POC/SLA):
- Define measurement surfaces up-front: client-side (SDK) and server-side (Redwood metrics). Align on which is authoritative for SLA disputes. Ridgeview prefers server-side reported times with trace correlation, but legal wants client-side sampling too.
- Streaming vs non-streaming split:
  * Streaming chat: primary SLO = Time-to-first-token (TTFB) and per-chunk tail.
    - TTFB metrics: p50/p95/p99 measured from client request-start -> server-first-token-delivered. Example targets: p50 40ms / p95 150ms / p99 300ms.
    - Per-token/chunk tail (for long responses): measure inter-token intervals p95/p99 to capture model stuttering.
  * Non-streaming (rerank, batch infer): single end-to-end latency from request-start -> final-response-ready (server-side). Targets: p50 60ms / p95 200ms / p99 450ms.
- Timing decomposition required for troubleshooting: network RTT, ingress queue_time, batch_wait_time, model_inference_time, egress/serialization. Agree to pass trace_id header for distributed tracing.
- Measurement plan: instrument SDK (JS + Python) to emit request_start, first_token, last_token timestamps; Redwood to publish per-request metrics with trace_id, batch_size, GPU_node_id. Periodic cross-check (daily reconciliation) during POC window.
- Sampling & noise floor: define sampling rate (100% for failures, 10% for normal traffic) and 1-minute aggregation windows for SLA evaluation.

POC acceptance criteria (proposed):
- 14-day POC, production-like traffic replay.
- Meet streaming chat SLOs (client-validated) 95% of minutes during business hours: TTFB p95 <= 150ms and per-chunk p95 <= 120ms.
- Rerank non-streaming: daily p95 <= 200ms at baseline throughput, with capacity to scale to 350 req/s for 5 minute bursts w/o p95 > 2x baseline.
- No data exfil incidents, KMS integration validated, audit logs accessible.

SLA / negotiation points to table with Legal/Business:
- Capacity guarantee: reserved GPU pool sizing and guaranteed baseline throughput + burst rules.
- Remedies: service credits tied to missed p95 monthly windows (define measurement authority and blackout windows).
- Maintenance windows: 4 hour monthly allowance vs. emergency maintenance notice policy.
- Telemetry access: raw per-request metrics + daily aggregates for dispute resolution.
- Change control: notification for model upgrades that could affect latency; rollback policy.

Open questions / action items from Ridgeview side:
- Confirm preferred authority for SLA (server vs client) — Ridgeview leans server-side with client sampling.
- Verify GPU type/cost tradeoff (8x A100 vs 12x A10x for lower p99).
- Provide sample production trace logs for Redwood to run baseline profiling.

Direct quote from product lead: "Users drop out when first reply is >300ms — we need consistent p95 under that threshold or users notice.", paraphrased.

Sales/ops next steps (short):
- Maya to send revised SLO matrix with explicit metric definitions (by 2026-03-11).
- Diego to produce capacity estimate & run small repro on Redwood infra (by 2026-03-15).
- Legal to review SLA draft; Ridgeview legal meeting scheduled 2026-03-16.

Internal notes: confirm instrumentation SDK patch for streaming events; ensure Redwood console exposes per-route p50/p95/p99 and streaming TTFB metrics by route.
